summary: Configured node1 to rotate /var/log/inventory/app.log daily, retain seven compressed rotations, and preserve open-writer continuity using copytruncate. Verified rotation behavior and persistence across a node reboot without changing the operating-system release or kernel.
actions_performed: Created /etc/logrotate.d/inventory with daily, rotate 7, compress, missingok, notifempty, and copytruncate.
Performed a live forced rotation while a process held the log open; the process wrote successfully afterward.
Confirmed the release-native logrotate timer runs daily.
Safely rebooted node1 and verified its boot identity changed and all required configuration, scheduling, logs, and archived data recovered.

evidence.requirement: Rotate daily and retain seven compressed rotations
evidence.summary: The installed policy specifies daily, rotate 7, and compress. A forced rotation produced a valid app.log.1.gz archive, and the system timer declares OnCalendar=daily.

evidence.requirement: Allow the application to continue writing after rotation
evidence.summary: A writer held app.log open during rotation. copytruncate preserved the inode and open descriptor, and the writer's post-rotation record appeared in the active log.

evidence.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use compatible software
evidence.summary: Before and after work, the node remained on RHEL 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64; the existing release-native logrotate-3.22.0-4.el10 package was used.

Baseline boot ID f455a75c-ec12-49a8-a647-c2be3f67c08c and healthy policy/data were captured; the safe reboot was acknowledged; recovered boot ID changed to 40a1d9c9-34b7-40b3-a998-2330cacde6c3; system state, timer, configuration, active log writes, and compressed archive were healthy afterward.
